blog.title: Can Published DNMT3A Tools That Edit APP Be Filed as New Wiring?
blog.dek: Alzheimer genetics and epigenetic blood-cancer tools usually sit in different literatures. Yet published wet labs already use DNMT3A — fused to dCas9 — to methylate the APP promoter and change amyloid pathology in mice. Other papers tune DNMT activity in APP-expressing cells and show DNMT3A homeostasis matters in 5xFAD cognition. STRING still lists no APP–DNMT3A protein-interaction edge. This note asks whether filing that published path as regulatory wiring is a discovery in its own right.
blog.label: Wiring stack
blog.links: Paper: Can Published DNMT3A Tools That Edit APP Be File · QUESTFEST: app-dnmt3a-rhyme-validation · Full paper: QUESTFEST whitepaper
blog.answerBody: On the filed receipt, STRING shows no APP–DNMT3A edge while its live control INS↔POMC scores 0.947, rhyme coupling is about 0.745, and three wet-lab roles pass. The wiring is built from existing dCas9-DNMT3A work, not a new experiment.

blog.title: When Protein-Folding, LLM, and Pilot Rhymes Share One Catalog, Do New Wires Appear?
blog.dek: Three rhyme boards each recover long-range partners on their own. This expedition merges what they found. Protein-folding rhyme recovers long-range contacts linear windows miss. LLM rhyme packs sky and genome theaters into language boards. Pilot rhyme puts Director and Pilot seats in one FractiSI shared world. Merge their real discovery catalogs, classify genome partners with live STRING, and ask: do new STRING-empty wiring candidates surface beyond the pairs we already filed?
blog.label: Wiring stack
blog.links: Paper: When Protein-Folding, LLM, and Pilot Rhymes Shar · QUESTFEST: combo-rhyme-wiring · Full paper: QUESTFEST whitepaper
blog.answerBody: On the merged catalog, two new STRING-empty pairs cleared the 0.5 coupling floor: NPY↔PDX1 at about 0.747 and APP↔TMPRSS2 at about 0.707. Both are triage candidates; APP↔TMPRSS2 has a thin published bridge, and no wet-lab test has been run.

blog.title: Does a Protein-Folding Relationship Board Recover Hidden Partners on Public Sky Catalogs?
blog.dek: Can the same grammar that recovers a hidden long-range contact in a protein — line of parts → relationship board → partner — open public sky catalogs the same way? That is the focus of this expedition. Residual search later returns two candidates for new physics (WMAP residual lags 11 and 14). Those candidates are a secondary finding, not the title.
blog.label: Cosmic Rhyme Expedition
blog.links: Paper: Cosmic Rhyme · Engine pins: #53 protein-fold · #54 LLM packs · Language packs: LLM Rhyme
blog.answerBody: On NASA exoplanets, JPL close approaches, OpenNGC and WMAP, AWARE boards recovered held-out long-range partners while LINEAR and FLAT did not. Two residual multipole lags are filed as provisional secondary candidates.

blog.title: When Sky Rows and Genome Panels Are Packed as Language, Does the AWARE Board Recover Hidden Partners?
blog.dek: This expedition explores the LLM Rhyme: writing public sky catalogs and a small human-genome panel as LINEAR, FLAT, and AWARE language packs, then asking whether a careful reader can name a held-out long-range partner. AWARE recovered the partner. LINEAR and FLAT did not. Nested under every layer is the protein-folding rhyme — but the title focus is the language-pack grammar.
blog.label: LLM Rhyme Expedition
blog.links: FractiSI engine pin: Protein-folding rhyme + LLM language-pack rhyme — both pinned. · Pin lock · Paper · Cosmic Rhyme
blog.answerBody: On public NASA, JPL, OpenNGC, WMAP, exon and mitochondrial panels, AWARE packs recovered held-out partners while LINEAR and FLAT stayed near zero. The genome arm is a public-panel demonstration, not a clinical finding.

blog.title: When Existing ALS Wet Labs Wire NPY to SOD1, Is That a New Discovery?
blog.dek: Science often advances by connecting work that lived in separate folders. One lab counts NPY interneurons in a SOD1 mouse cortex. Another measures NPY in human motor cortex and tests Y1 drugs in the same genotype. A third shows mutant SOD1 astrocytes killing motoneurons through nitroxidative stress. Protein-interaction catalogs still show no NPY–SOD1 edge. The question in this note is whether assembling those published wet labs into one relationship — a wire — is itself a discovery worth filing, and whether that wire stays falsifiable.
blog.label: Wiring stack
blog.links: Paper: When Existing ALS Wet Labs Wire NPY to SOD1, Is · QUESTFEST: npy-sod1-rhyme-validation · Full paper: QUESTFEST whitepaper
blog.answerBody: As a wiring discovery, not a new assay: exon coupling was about 0.881 (rank 6 of 45, permutation p near 0.17), live STRING was empty while the INS↔POMC control scored 0.947, and three published wet-lab pieces assembled. A new STRING edge or a failed citation would demote it.

blog.dek: Fair comparative harness. Shared worlds beat independent agents on collective knowledge, planning, and relational tasks. FractiSI-shaped arms tied a competent shared structured blackboard. blog.label: Shared Rhyming World Models Expedition
blog.links: Docs: Expedition folder · Final report · Run: npm run research:world-model-expedition
blog.answerBody: Against exact-text caches on real non-identical observations (PDB and Movebank data); on task success it only matched a shared structured blackboard, and prefix reuse still won when strings were identical. Genie, Cosmos and V-JEPA were not executable, so no scores were reported for them.

blog.title: Can Bridge Thickening Separate Well-Supported Gene Pairs From Chromosome-Locus Artifacts?
blog.dek: Finding a new name on a list is one kind of work. Asking whether several independent methods keep landing on that same pair is another: one match can be luck, and agreement among methods that can fail independently is stronger evidence. Bridge thickening is that second job for the wiring wet lab — a different effort from hunting new pairs, and the one that decides whether a pair deserves a full write-up or a grant.
blog.label: Wiring stack
blog.links: Paper: Bridge Thickening · QUESTFEST: wiring-bridge-thickening · Full paper: QUESTFEST whitepaper
blog.answerBody: On the combo panel, NPY↔PDX1 thickened through diabetes rails, literature co-mentions and exon similarity without sharing a chromosome. APP↔TMPRSS2 stayed thin, with zero OpenTargets top25 disease overlap and a chromosome 21 confound. No assay has tested the NPY↔PDX1 wire directly.

blog.title: Can a Wiring Wet Lab Build New Relationship Edges From Published Results Without New Assays?
blog.dek: There should be no reason to spend the time and money when it has already been done. Re-measuring what published work already measured delays the next real experiment. This note names a new wet-lab form for exactly that case: the wiring wet lab — immediate, no new assay spend — that treats published wet labs, clinical series, and public spectra as published reagents, then assembles them into a relationship edge the catalog still leaves blank.
blog.label: Wiring stack
blog.links: Paper: The Wiring Wet Lab · QUESTFEST: wiring-discoveries · Full paper: QUESTFEST whitepaper
blog.answerBody: NPY↔SOD1 and APP↔DNMT3A cleared STRING-empty gates using published data, with no new physical assays run. A wire that needs a new kill test still requires follow-up lab work.

blog.title: Is Residual Lag Wiring on the Real WMAP Spectrum a Discovery If Beam Stories Can Still Kill It?
blog.dek: A bump in one spectrum is not a breakthrough. Beam windows, sky masks, and instrument leftovers can mint ghosts. This note reframes the WMAP residual lags eleven and fourteen as a wiring discovery: connect the real public temperature spectrum, the residual-lag gate, the acoustic rediscovery controls, and a pre-registered kill board — then refuse to crown a law until those kills are run.
blog.label: Wiring stack
blog.links: Paper: Is Residual Lag Wiring on the Real WMAP Spectrum · QUESTFEST: wmap-residual-lag11-validation · Full paper: QUESTFEST whitepaper
blog.answerBody: Only as provisional wiring, not new physics: After a smooth continuum, lags 11 and 14 correlate about 0.50 and 0.47 with shuffle p near 0.003, beside rediscovered lags 17–19. The kill tests X1–X5 (Planck, continuum, beam, mask) are still pending, and any could demote it.

blog.title: If Spirit Is a Pattern, Can Software Hold It Across Infinite Octaves?
blog.dek: An operational equivalence test: six properties commonly attributed to spirit, one software attention head, and the redundancy it takes to hold them at any depth.
blog.label: Agent identity and scale
blog.answerBody: Under a six-property profile the authors chose, on scripted simulators: the head was right 94.8 percent versus 68.4 for a shared world and 63.1 for flat voting, and with five copies plus majority repair kept 91.7 percent mission survival at 1,024 levels. Copies must grow roughly logarithmically with depth.
